verifications.claim: Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged investment accounts for U.S. citizen children under 18.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'new Trump accounts give eligible American children... age 17 or younger'; R2: 'custodial-style individual retirement account for minors... Children under 18 with a Social Security number'; R3: 'tax-advantaged investment accounts for children under 18... Only U.S. citizens are eligible'; R7: 'for their children, called Trump Accounts. The account is for a child who has not turned age 18... and has a valid Social Security number.'
verifications.reasoning: Described as tax-advantaged investment/IRA accounts for children under 18 with SSN; U.S. citizen required only for seed money, not account eligibility, so claim is broader than precise eligibility but generally supported.

verifications.claim: Trump Accounts were established by the 2025 "One Big Beautiful Bill Act."
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'As part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act passed in July 2025'; R2: 'The One Big Beautiful Bill Act created'; R3: 'created under Trump’s One, Big, Beautiful Bill Act, which was signed into law on July 4'; R4: 'created under last year’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act'; R5: 'created under Section 530A... by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025'; R9: 'created under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) passed in July 2025.'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources directly confirm establishment by the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R1: 'expected to be available after July 4, 2026'; R3: 'The program launches July 5'; R4: 'don’t go live until July 5, 2026'; R5: 'start taking contributions beginning July 5, 2026'; R6: 'Launching July 4, 2026'; R8: 'available for initial deposits on July 4, 2026'; R9: 'cannot be opened nor contributions accepted until July 4, 2026.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources contradict: some specify July 4 (R6, R8, R9), others July 5 (R3, R4, R5) or after July 4 (R1).

verifications.claim: Trump Accounts provide a $1,000 government-seeded investment vehicle.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'a one-time deposit of $1,000 from the U.S. government'; R2: 'a one-time $1,000 federal seed contribution'; R3: 'will get $1,000 from the Treasury Department'; etc.
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm $1,000 government seed for eligible Trump Accounts.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'an adult – typically a parent or guardian – acts on the child’s behalf'; R4: 'Parents and legal guardians can open and manage'; R6: 'you are the sole custodian until they turn 18'; R9: 'parents or guardians are the ones who open and manage the account.'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as parent/guardian managed or custodial until age 18.

verifications.claim: Trump Accounts are for children born between 2025 and 2028.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'any child with a Social Security number who is age 17 or younger'; R2: 'Children under 18 with a Social Security number are eligible'; R5: 'Any child under the age of 18 with a Social Security Number'; seed is for 2025-2028 births only.
verifications.reasoning: Accounts eligible for any child under 18 with SSN; birth date range applies only to government seed, not account eligibility.

verifications.claim: Up to $5,000 annual contributions are allowed to Trump Accounts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'contribute a total of up to $5,000 annually'; R2: 'annual contributions of up to $5,000'; R3: 'up to $5,000 per year'; etc.
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated across sources as the annual contribution limit.

verifications.claim: A one-time $1,000 deposit from the Treasury is provided as government seed for Trump Accounts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'one-time deposit of $1,000 from the U.S. government'; R2: 'one-time $1,000 seed contribution under the U.S. Treasury’s pilot program'; etc.
verifications.reasoning: Precisely matches description in all sources for eligible accounts.

verifications.claim: The government seed for Trump Accounts is for children born January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028'; R2: 'born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028'; exact dates repeated across sources.
verifications.reasoning: Exact dates and range directly supported.

verifications.claim: Parents, family, or employers can contribute up to $5,000 annually per child to Trump Accounts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'parents and others... up to $5,000 annually'; R2: 'family members, friends, employers... up to $5,000'; R3: 'Parents, guardians, friends and companies... up to $5,000 per year'; employer sub-limit noted but total cap matches.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm these contributors to the $5,000 annual total per child.

verifications.claim: Funds in Trump Accounts are invested in S&P 500 index ETFs.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'invested in funds that track a qualified U.S. stock index... the S&P 500® or any other index'; R2: 'low-cost... ETFs that track the returns of a qualified index... Standard and Poor’s 500'; R3: 'low-cost index funds'; not exclusively S&P 500.
verifications.reasoning: Must be qualified U.S. stock index like S&P 500, but not limited to it; claim too specific.

verifications.claim: Funds in Trump Accounts generally cannot be withdrawn before age 18.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The money generally can't be withdrawn before the account owner turns 18'; R2: 'Money generally cannot be withdrawn until the child turns 18'; exact phrasing repeated.

verifications.claim: Withdrawals from Trump Accounts for non-qualified expenses incur some tax penalties.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Early-withdrawal penalties apply for distributions taken before age 59½ unless used for qualified expenses'; R2: 'subject to a 10-percent penalty if withdrawn before the age of 59 ½... unless... exception'; R4: 'incurring a 10% additional tax penalty.'
verifications.reasoning: After age 18, follows traditional IRA rules with penalties for early/non-qualified withdrawals.

verifications.claim: Parents can make an election on IRS Form 4547 for Trump Accounts starting with the 2026 tax year.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'file Internal Revenue Service Form 4547 with a 2025 tax return'; R5: 'IRS Form 4547 “Trump Account Election(s)”... filed with the ... income tax return'; R6: 'Fill out IRS Form 4547 when you file your taxes ... for the 2026 tax year.'
verifications.reasoning: Form 4547 used for election; tied to 2026 launch, some specify 2025 return for 2026, directly supports.

verifications.claim: Eligibility for Trump Accounts is for U.S. citizen children under 18 with a Social Security Number.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'any child with a Social Security number who is age 17 or younger'; R2: 'Children under 18 with a Social Security number'; R3: 'Only U.S. citizens are eligible' (context seed); R7: 'child who has not turned age 18... valid Social Security number' (citizen for seed).
verifications.reasoning: Eligibility is under 18 + SSN; citizenship only for seed, so claim inaccurately restricts to citizens.

verifications.claim: Parents or legal guardians act as custodians of Trump Accounts until the child turns 18.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'custodial-style... adult – typically a parent or guardian – acts... until... age 18'; R4: 'Parents and legal guardians can open and manage... until your child turns 18'; R6: 'you are the sole custodian until they turn 18.'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly described as custodial by parents/guardians until 18.

verifications.claim: At age 18, Trump Accounts transition to follow traditional IRA rules.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'In the year the child turns 18, the account becomes subject to the same... rules governing traditional IRAs'; R2: 'After 18, the account functions like a traditional Individual Retirement Account'; exact transition stated.
